Mosedis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klaipėda County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Mosedis's Jewish community grew after Jews received formal settlement rights in the Žemaitija region in 1742, peaking at 363 people (40 percent of the town) by the late 19th century. All nine of the town's businesses were Jewish-owned by 1931. In 1941, Jewish men were sent to Skuodas and killed there, while women and children were taken to the Jewish cemetery in Kretinga and shot — though some Jewish youths escaped to Russia and survived. Professor Moshe-Zvi Segal, a biblical scholar born in Mosedis, later taught at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. This cemetery, established in the second half of the 18th century on a hill near two rivers' confluence, lost many gravestones to theft and vandalism under Soviet rule; after a dam was built on the Bartuva river in 1972, the cemetery became surrounded by an artificial pond, leaving it stranded on an island to this day.
